name: General Python Placement Assessment
description: A 40-question multiple-choice placement test spanning the full Python Apprentice and Python Games concept range. Used to place a prospective student into the right course and starting lesson.

placement_rubric.explanation: Score each band as a percentage of its questions answered correctly. Walk the bands in order; the student is placed at the START of the first band scoring below the mastery threshold. If every band is mastered, use 'placed_beyond'.

placed_beyond.note: Mastered all assessed Python content — ready for Python Games projects or the next level (Java). Recommend instructor review.

questions.question: What does turtle programming let you do?
options: Give commands to a virtual turtle telling it where to move and draw
Connect to the internet to download images
Edit photos taken with a camera
questions.answer: Give commands to a virtual turtle telling it where to move and draw
questions.explanation: Turtle programming lets you control a virtual turtle that draws on the screen, like a small robot artist.

questions.question: Where does the turtle module come from?
options: It is a pre-installed Python tool
You must buy it from a store
You build it yourself before class
It only works on the League Code Server
questions.answer: It is a pre-installed Python tool
questions.explanation: The lesson explains the turtle module is a pre-installed Python tool you use to control the turtle.

questions.question: Which file extension belongs to a notebook file?
questions.answer: .ipynb
questions.explanation: Notebook files end with .ipynb and let you read text and run code in the same document.

questions.question: Which file extension belongs to a standalone Python program?
questions.answer: .py
questions.explanation: Python files end with .py and you can run them by clicking the play button.

questions.question: What is a code cell in a notebook?
options: A box where you can write and run code
A note for humans that the computer ignores
The icon that opens the virtual screen
A type of variable that stores numbers
questions.answer: A box where you can write and run code
questions.explanation: A code cell is simply a box in a notebook where you write code and run it.

questions.question: Besides clicking the play button, which keyboard shortcut runs a code cell?
questions.answer: Shift + Enter
questions.explanation: You can run a cell by clicking the play button or by pressing Shift + Enter.

questions.question: In the assignment, how do you change what gets printed so it shows your name instead of 'Hello World!'?
options: Change the text inside the quotation marks
Rename the file to your name
questions.answer: Change the text inside the quotation marks
questions.explanation: The string inside the quotes is the text printed, so editing it changes the output.

questions.question: Why might nothing visible happen the first time you press the play button?
options: You still need to pick which Python interpreter to use
The turtle ran out of ink
questions.answer: You still need to pick which Python interpreter to use
questions.explanation: Until you choose an interpreter, the code cannot run, so you see no result.

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: Both values are strings, so + concatenates them into "1020".

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: Both values are integers, so + does arithmetic addition.

questions.question: What happens when you run this code?
questions.answer: Raises a TypeError
questions.explanation: You can't add an integer to a string directly, so Python raises a TypeError.

questions.question: What is the value of 11 // 4?
questions.explanation: Floor division of two integers drops the decimal and returns an integer, 2.

questions.question: What is the value of 11 % 4?
questions.explanation: 4 goes into 11 twice with 3 left over, so the remainder is 3.

questions.question: What does print(22 / 7) display?
questions.explanation: Regular division with / always produces a float, even with integers.

questions.question: What does print(22.0 // 7.0) display?
questions.explanation: Floor division with floats keeps the float type, giving 3.0.

questions.question: Which expression converts the string "20" so it can be added to the integer 10 to get 30?
questions.explanation: int("20") turns the string into the integer 20, so the result is 30.

questions.question: What is an iterable?
options: Anything that can produce its items one at a time until nothing is left
A number that can only be used inside a loop
A special kind of variable that counts upward
A function that always returns True
questions.answer: Anything that can produce its items one at a time until nothing is left
questions.explanation: An iterable lets you get the first item, then the next, until none remain.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT given as an example of an iterable in this lesson?
questions.answer: An integer like 42
questions.explanation: Lists, tuples, strings, and ranges are iterables; a plain integer is not.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: range(10) produces 0 through 9, and list() collects them.

questions.question: What is the result of list("abc")?
questions.explanation: Strings are iterable, so list() splits the string into individual characters.

questions.question: What is the correct general structure of a for loop?
questions.answer: for <variable> in <iterable>:
questions.explanation: A for loop is the for keyword, a variable, in, an iterable, then a colon.

questions.question: How many lines does this loop print?
questions.explanation: The list has four items, so the loop runs four times, printing four lines.

questions.question: What does this loop print first?
questions.answer: H
questions.explanation: Looping over a string yields one character at a time, starting with the first, H.

questions.question: What is an infinite loop?
options: A loop that runs forever because it has no termination condition
A loop that runs exactly 100 times
A loop with more than one variable
questions.answer: A loop that runs forever because it has no termination condition
questions.explanation: Without a way to stop, or with an endless iterable, the loop never ends.

questions.question: In a function definition, where does the function's name appear?
questions.answer: Right after the def keyword
questions.explanation: The name comes right after def, as in def add_ten(x).

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.code:
def add_ten(x):
    return x + 10

result = add_ten(5)
print(result)
questions.explanation: add_ten(5) returns 5 + 10, which is 15.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.code:
def do_nothing():
    pass

result = do_nothing()
print("Return value:", result)
questions.answer: Return value: None
questions.explanation: do_nothing has no return statement, so it returns None.

questions.question: Given def greet_user(name, greeting), what does greet_user(greeting="Hello", name="Alice") print?
options: An error, because the order is wrong
questions.answer: Hello, Alice!
questions.explanation: Keyword arguments are matched by name, so order does not matter.

questions.question: When mixing positional and keyword arguments in a function call, which rule must you follow?
options: Positional arguments must come before keyword arguments
They must be in alphabetical order
questions.answer: Positional arguments must come before keyword arguments
questions.explanation: You cannot place a positional argument after a keyword argument.

questions.question: Given def greet_user(name, greeting), what happens when you run greet_user(name="Bob", greeting)?
options: A SyntaxError, because a positional argument follows a keyword argument
questions.answer: A SyntaxError, because a positional argument follows a keyword argument
questions.explanation: You cannot put a positional argument after a keyword argument.

questions.question: What does greet_user("Alice") print with this definition?
questions.answer: Hello, Alice!
questions.explanation: greeting and punct use their defaults 'Hello' and '!'.

questions.question: Which statement about default parameter values is true?
options: Parameters with defaults must come after parameters without defaults
Parameters with defaults must come first
Every parameter must have a default
questions.answer: Parameters with defaults must come after parameters without defaults
questions.explanation: Required parameters come before optional ones with defaults.

questions.question: In a Pygame physics program, what does acceleration directly change?
questions.answer: The velocity
questions.explanation: Acceleration is added to velocity each frame, and velocity then changes position.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the relationship between a class and an object?
options: A class is a copy of an object
A class is a blueprint and an object is built from it
An object is a blueprint for a class
They are exactly the same thing
questions.answer: A class is a blueprint and an object is built from it
questions.explanation: A class defines the type; an object is one instance made from that blueprint.

questions.question: What does a 2D vector contain?
options: An x value and a y value
questions.answer: An x value and a y value
questions.explanation: A 2D vector groups an x and a y together into one object.

questions.question: What is a sprite in Pygame?
options: A 2D image that represents a game object
questions.answer: A 2D image that represents a game object
questions.explanation: Sprites are the images that move around the screen.

questions.question: What are the three types of collision detection described in the lesson?
options: Bounding box, circle, and pixel perfect
questions.answer: Bounding box, circle, and pixel perfect
questions.explanation: These are the three approaches the lesson lists.

questions.question: According to the lesson, a surface is best compared to what?
options: A blank piece of paper you can draw on
questions.answer: A blank piece of paper you can draw on
questions.explanation: A surface is anything you can draw on, including the screen and images.

questions.question: What kind of motion does this code produce for the red square?
questions.code:
a = (-K * (x_pos - center)) / mass
velocity += a * d_t
x_pos += velocity * d_t
options: It moves at a constant speed forever
It oscillates back and forth around the center like it is attached to a spring
questions.answer: It oscillates back and forth around the center like it is attached to a spring
questions.explanation: The acceleration always points back toward the center, producing spring-like oscillation.

questions.question: Given the Person class, which line creates a Person object named Alice who is 14?
questions.answer: alice = Person("Alice", 14)
questions.explanation: Calling the class like a function runs __init__ and builds the object.
